description: This classic Chinese Hot and Sour Soup delivers a perfect balance of savory, tangy, and spicy flavors, making it a beloved comfort food. Loaded with tender pork, silky tofu, and various mushrooms, each spoonful offers a delightful textural contrast. Its aromatic broth, seasoned with vinegar and white pepper, is incredibly invigorating and satisfying.

ingredients.notes: freshly ground, plus more to taste
mixed with 6 tbsp cold water for slurry

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rehydrate dried shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in separate bowls of hot water for 20 minutes, then drain, squeeze dry, remove stems from shiitake, and shred both types of mushrooms thinly. Shred pork loin, firm tofu, and bamboo shoots into similar thin strips. Prepare the cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch with cold water in a small bowl. Beat the egg in another small bowl.

instructions.title: Cook Pork and Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat a large pot or wok over medium-high heat. Add a touch of cooking oil and stir-fry the shredded pork until it changes color and is no longer pink. Remove pork and set aside. In the same pot, add the shredded shiitake and wood ear mushrooms, and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Add the shredded bamboo shoots and cook for another minute.

instructions.title: Simmer the Broth
instructions.text: Pour in the chicken broth into the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. Add the cooked pork back into the pot. Let it simmer gently for about 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Season the Soup
instructions.text: Stir in the rice vinegar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and white pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed, adding more vinegar or white pepper for your preferred level of hot and sour. Add the shredded firm tofu to the simmering soup.

instructions.title: Thicken and Add Egg
instructions.text: Stir the cornstarch slurry well, then slowly pour it into the simmering soup in a thin stream while continuously stirring. Continue stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. Once thickened, slowly drizzle the beaten egg into the hot soup in a thin stream, stirring gently in one direction to create delicate egg ribbons. Cook for about 30 seconds until the egg is set.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the pot from heat. Stir in the sesame oil. Ladle the hot and sour soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish generously with sliced green onions. For an extra kick, a drizzle of chili oil can be added to each bowl before serving. Serve immediately and enjoy!

tips: For authentic flavor, use freshly ground white pepper generously; it provides the signature 'hot' element. Do not substitute with black pepper.
The balance of sourness and spiciness is key. Always taste and adjust the rice vinegar and white pepper at the end to suit your preference.
If you want to make this vegetarian, simply omit the pork and use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth. The soup is still delicious and hearty.
article:
Hot and Sour Soup is a culinary masterpiece, a vibrant symphony of flavors that has captivated palates worldwide. This iconic Chinese soup, known for its distinct tangy and spicy profile, offers a comforting yet exhilarating experience with every spoonful. Whether you've enjoyed it at your favorite Chinese restaurant or are discovering its magic for the first time, learning to make this delicious dish at home is a rewarding journey. It's more than just a starter; it's a testament to the intricate balance of flavors that defines Chinese cuisine.

In this comprehensive guide, we'll dive deep into the world of Hot and Sour Soup, exploring its origins, breaking down its essential ingredients, and providing a clear, step-by-step Hot and Sour Soup recipe that even novice cooks can master. Get ready to embark on a flavorful adventure that will transform your kitchen into a haven of aromatic delights.

## What is Hot and Sour Soup?

At its heart, Hot and Sour Soup (酸辣汤 – suān là tāng) is a traditional Chinese soup characterized by its intriguing balance of piquant and tangy notes. The "hot" comes from ingredients like white pepper and chili oil, while the "sour" is typically derived from Chinese black vinegar. Beyond these dominant flavors, the soup is rich in umami, often featuring a medley of ingredients such as shredded pork, tofu, mushrooms (shiitake and wood ear are common), bamboo shoots, and sometimes egg ribbons. Its thick, velvety texture, achieved by a cornstarch slurry, adds to its satisfying mouthfeel.

Originating from the northern regions of China, particularly Sichuan and Hunan provinces, it embodies the regional preference for bold, spicy, and sour flavors. However, countless variations exist across China and beyond, each offering a slightly different interpretation of this beloved classic. It’s a soup that awakens the senses, stimulating the appetite and providing a comforting warmth, making it a staple on menus from casual eateries to upscale dining establishments.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Hot and Sour Soup

Crafting an authentic Hot and Sour Soup recipe requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients, many of which are readily available in Asian grocery stores or even well-stocked supermarkets. Here’s a breakdown of what you’ll need to create this flavor-packed dish:

*   **For the Broth:**
    *   6-8 cups chicken or vegetable broth (low sodium preferred)
*   **Proteins:**
    *   4-6 oz pork tenderloin or chicken breast, thinly sliced or shredded
    *   8 oz firm or extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into small strips
*   **Vegetables & Fungi:**
    *   1/2 cup bamboo shoots, shredded
    *   1/4 cup dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced
    *   1/4 cup dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrated and thinly sliced
*   **Flavor Base & Seasonings:**
    *   2 tbsp soy sauce (light or regular)
    *   3-4 tbsp Chinese black vinegar (Chinkiang vinegar is ideal)
    *   1-2 tbsp white pepper (freshly ground for best flavor)
    *   1-2 tsp sesame oil
    *   1-2 tsp chili oil (optional, for extra heat)
    *   1/2 tsp sugar (to balance flavors)
    *   1-2 cloves garlic, minced (optional)
    *   1 tsp fresh ginger, grated (optional)
*   **Thickener & Garnish:**
    *   2 large eggs, beaten
    *   3-4 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with 1/4 cup cold water (cornstarch slurry)
    *   2-3 green onions, thinly sliced (for garnish)
    *   Fresh cilantro, chopped (optional garnish)

Having these components ready is the first step to a successful Hot and Sour Soup recipe.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Hot and Sour Soup

Making your own Hot and Sour Soup is surprisingly straightforward and incredibly rewarding. Follow these steps to prepare a delicious batch:

1.  **Prepare Ingredients:** Begin by rehydrating your dried mushrooms according to package directions, then slice them thinly. Slice the pork or chicken into thin strips. Press your tofu and cut it into small, uniform pieces. Prepare your bamboo shoots and other garnishes.
2.  **Cook the Protein:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, bring your broth to a simmer. Add the thinly sliced pork or chicken and cook until it's just done, about 2-3 minutes. Skim any foam that rises to the surface.
3.  **Add Vegetables and Flavorings:** Stir in the rehydrated shiitake and wood ear mushrooms, bamboo shoots, and tofu. Add the soy sauce, Chinese black vinegar, white pepper, sugar, and optional garlic and ginger. Bring the soup back to a gentle simmer and let it cook for 5-7 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
4.  **Thicken the Soup:** Give your cornstarch slurry a quick stir to ensure the cornstarch hasn't settled. Slowly pour the slurry into the simmering soup in a thin, steady stream, stirring continuously. Continue stirring until the soup thickens to your desired consistency. If it's too thick, add a little more broth; if too thin, mix a bit more cornstarch with water and add.
5.  **Incorporate Eggs:** Once the soup has thickened, slowly drizzle the beaten eggs into the simmering soup in a circular motion. Let the egg cook for about 30 seconds without stirring, then gently stir once or twice to create delicate egg ribbons.
6.  **Finish and Serve:** Remove the pot from the heat. Stir in the sesame oil and chili oil (if using). Taste and adjust seasonings as needed – perhaps a little more vinegar for tang, more white pepper for heat, or a dash of salt. Ladle the hot soup into bowls and garnish generously with sliced green onions and fresh cilantro. This Hot and Sour Soup recipe is now ready to be enjoyed!

## Tips for the Best Hot and Sour Soup

Achieving that perfect balance of hot and sour, savory and umami, is key to an outstanding Hot and Sour Soup. Here are some tips to elevate your homemade rendition:

*   **Don't Skimp on the Vinegar and Pepper:** These are the stars! Use good quality Chinese black vinegar (Chinkiang is highly recommended for its complex, slightly sweet flavor). For the "hot," white pepper is traditional and provides a unique pungent warmth; don't substitute it entirely with chili flakes if you want authentic flavor. Adjust quantities to your personal preference.
*   **Balance is Key:** After adding all ingredients, taste the soup and adjust. If it's too sour, a pinch of sugar can balance it. If not hot enough, add more white pepper or chili oil. If it tastes flat, a splash more soy sauce or a dash of salt might be needed.
*   **Proper Thickening:** Ensure your cornstarch slurry is well-mixed before adding to prevent lumps. Add it slowly while stirring to control the thickness. You want a velvety texture, not a gluey one.
*   **Egg Ribbons:** For delicate egg ribbons, make sure the soup is simmering gently, not boiling vigorously, when you drizzle in the beaten egg. Let it set for a moment before stirring gently.
*   **Fresh Ingredients:** While dried mushrooms are essential for depth, fresh ingredients like quality broth, fresh pork/chicken, and vibrant green onions make a noticeable difference in the final flavor.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Hot and Sour Soup is a fantastic starter on its own, but it also pairs wonderfully with a variety of Chinese dishes. Serve it piping hot in individual bowls, garnished with fresh green onions and a drizzle of extra chili oil for those who like more heat.

It complements rich, savory main courses beautifully, as its acidity and spice cut through fattiness and cleanse the palate. Consider serving it alongside dishes like General Tso's Chicken, Beef with Broccoli, or a simple fried rice. For a lighter meal, enjoy it with some steamed dumplings or spring rolls. A warm cup of jasmine tea makes an excellent beverage pairing.

## Hot and Sour Soup Variations & Substitutions

One of the joys of cooking is customization, and this Hot and Sour Soup recipe is incredibly adaptable.

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Omit the pork and use vegetable broth. Ensure your soy sauce is vegan-friendly. Increase the amount of tofu and add other vegetables like shredded carrots or cabbage.
*   **Different Proteins:** Instead of pork or chicken, try shrimp, shredded duck, or even thinly sliced beef.
*   **Mushroom Variety:** Experiment with other dried mushrooms like oyster mushrooms for different textures and flavors.
*   **Spice Level:** For more heat, add dried red chili flakes, a dash of sriracha, or increase the amount of chili oil. For less heat, reduce the white pepper.
*   **Gluten-Free:** Use tamari instead of soy sauce and ensure your broth is gluten-free. Cornstarch is naturally gluten-free.
*   **Extra Umami:** A touch of mushroom powder or MSG (monosodium glutamate) can enhance the savory depth of your Hot and Sour Soup recipe.

Hot and Sour Soup is a beloved classic for good reason. Its dynamic flavors and comforting warmth make it a truly satisfying dish. By following this detailed Hot and Sour Soup recipe and incorporating our tips, you’re well on your way to mastering this iconic Chinese staple in your own kitchen. Enjoy the process, savor the aroma, and delight in the incredible taste of your homemade creation!
